arxiv-1809-06785.title: Turbulent and adaptive optics corrected point-spread functions as convolutive orders of the phase power spectral density 2018 Turbulent and adaptive optics corrected point-spread functions as convolutive orders of the phase power spectral density – 7
arxiv-1809-06785.creator: Romain JL. Fétick, Benoit Neichel, Laurent M Mugnier, Aurélie Montmerle-Bonnefois, Thierry Fusco
arxiv-1809-06785.description: Abstract Ground-based astronomy is severely limited by the atmospheric turbulence, resulting in a large Point-Spread-Function (PSF) and poor imaging resolution. Even imaging with Adaptive Optics (AO) cannot completely correct the aberrated wavefront, and a residual turbulence still corrupts the observation. Thus the consequences of the turbulence on the PSF is of first interest when building any ground-based telescope.

arxiv-2108-01998.title: Adversarial Energy Disaggregation for Non-intrusive Load Monitoring Journal: TDS CCS: Applied computing Industry and manufacturing CCS: Information systems Data mining CCS: Information systems Data streaming
arxiv-2108-01998.creator: Zhekai Du, Jingjing Li, Lei Zhu, Ke Lu, Heng Tao Shen
arxiv-2108-01998.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zhekai Du, Jingjing Li, Lei Zhu, Ke Lu, Heng Tao Shen. Energy disaggregation, also known as non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM), challenges the problem of separating the whole-home electricity usage into appliance-specific individual consumptions, which is a typical application of data analysis.

arxiv-2310-03395.title: Returns to the origin of the Pólya walk with stochastic resetting
arxiv-2310-03395.creator: Claude Godrèche, Jean-Marc Luck*
arxiv-2310-03395.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Claude Godrèche, Jean-Marc Luck*. We consider the simple random walk (or Pólya walk) on the one-dimensional lattice subject to stochastic resetting to the origin with probability r r at each time step. The focus is on the joint statistics of the numbers 𝒩 t × {\mathcal{N}}_{t}^{\times} of spontaneous returns of the walker to the origin and 𝒩 t ∙ {\mathcal{N}}_{t}^{\bullet} of resetting events up to some observation time t t .

arxiv-2405-10259.title: Energy-limited quantum dynamics
arxiv-2405-10259.creator: Lauritz van Luijk
arxiv-2405-10259.description: Abstract We consider quantum systems with energy constraints. In general, quantum channels and continuous-time dynamics need not satisfy energy conservation. Physically meaningful channels, however, can only introduce a finite amount of energy to the system, and continuous-time dynamics may only increase the energy gradually over time. We systematically study such “energy-limited” channels and dynamics.

arxiv-2408-11639.title: Capture Rates of Highly Degenerate Neutrons Journal: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.
arxiv-2408-11639.creator: B. Knight, O. L. Caballero, H. Schatz
arxiv-2408-11639.description: Abstract At the low temperature and high density conditions of a neutron star crust neutrons are degenerate. In this work, we study the effect of this degeneracy on the capture rates of neutrons on neutron rich nuclei in accreted crusts. We use a statistical Hauser-Feshbach model to calculate neutron capture rates and find that neutron degeneracy can increase rates significantly.

arxiv-2409-15281.title: LAAG-RV: LLM Assisted Assertion Generation for RTL Design Verification
arxiv-2409-15281.creator: Karthik Maddala, Bhabesh Mali, Chandan Karfa
arxiv-2409-15281.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Karthik Maddala, Bhabesh Mali, Chandan Karfa. Writing SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) is an important but complex step in verifying Register Transfer Level (RTL) designs. Conventionally, experts need to understand the design specifications and write the SVA assertions, which is time-consuming and error-prone. However, with the recent advancement of transformer models, the Large Language Models (LLMs) assisted assertion generation for design verification is gaining interest in recent times.

arxiv-2410-21099.title: H 2 − H 2 ​ O \rm H_{2}-H_{2}O demixing in Uranus and Neptune: Adiabatic structure models
arxiv-2410-21099.creator: M. Cano Amoros, N. Nettelmann, N. Tosi, P. Baumeister, H. Rauer
arxiv-2410-21099.description: Abstract Context. Demixing properties of planetary major constituents influence the interior structure and evolution of planets. Comparing experimental and computational data on the miscibility of hydrogen and water to adiabatic profiles suggests phase separation between these two components occurs in the ice giants Uranus and Neptune. Aims.

arxiv-2502-21033.title: A data augmentation strategy for deep neural networks with application to epidemic modelling
arxiv-2502-21033.creator: Muhammad Awais, Abu Safyan Ali, Giacomo Dimarco, Federica Ferrarese, Lorenzo Pareschi
arxiv-2502-21033.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Muhammad Awais, Abu Safyan Ali, Giacomo Dimarco, Federica Ferrarese, Lorenzo Pareschi. In this work, we integrate the predictive capabilities of compartmental disease dynamics models with machine learning’s ability to analyze complex, high-dimensional data and uncover patterns that conventional models may overlook. Specifically, we present a proof of concept demonstrating the application of data-driven methods and deep neural networks to a recently introduced Susceptible-Infected-Recovered type model with social features, including a saturated incidence rate, to improve epidemic prediction and forecasting.

arxiv-2504-00078.title: Holographic Interfaces in Symmetric Product Orbifolds
arxiv-2504-00078.creator: Sebastian Harris, Yasuaki Hikida, Volker Schomerus, and Takashi Tsuda
arxiv-2504-00078.description: Abstract The study of non-local operators in gauge theory and holography, such as line-operators or interfaces, has attracted significant attention. Two-dimensional symmetric product orbifolds are close cousins of higher-dimensional gauge theory. In this work, we construct a novel family of interfaces in symmetric product orbifolds.

arxiv-2504-15335.title: Plasma Instabilities Dominate Radioactive Transients Magnetic Fields: The self-confinement of leptons in Type Ia and Core-Collapse Supernovae, and Kilonovae
arxiv-2504-15335.creator: Dhvanil D. Desai, Colby C. Haggerty, Benjamin J. Shappee, Michael A. Tucker, Zachary Davis, Chris Ashall, Laura Chomiuk, Keyan Gootkin, Damiano Caprioli, Antoine Bret, Hayk Hakobyan
arxiv-2504-15335.description: Abstract The light curves of radioactive transients, such as supernovae and kilonovae, are powered by the decay of radioisotopes, which release high-energy leptons through β + \beta^{+} and β − \beta^{-} decays. These leptons deposit energy into the expanding ejecta. As the ejecta density decreases during expansion, the plasma becomes collisionless, with particle motion governed by electromagnetic forces.

arxiv-2505-04996.title: Inter - Diffusion Generation Model of Speakers and Listeners for Effective Communication
arxiv-2505-04996.creator: Jinhe Huang, Yongkang Cheng, Minghang Yu*, Gaoge Han, Jinwei Li, Jing Zhang, Shilei Wang, Xingjian Gu
arxiv-2505-04996.description: Abstract . Full-body gestures play a pivotal role in natural interactions and are crucial for achieving effective communication. Nevertheless, most existing studies primarily focus on the gesture generation of speakers, overlooking the vital role of listeners in the interaction process and failing to fully explore the dynamic interaction between them.

arxiv-2601-02441.title: Understanding Pure Textual Reasoning for Blind Image Quality Assessment
arxiv-2601-02441.creator: Yuan Li, Shin’ya Nishida
arxiv-2601-02441.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yuan Li, Shin’ya Nishida. Textual reasoning has recently been widely adopted in Blind Image Quality Assessment (BIQA). However, it remains unclear how textual information contributes to quality prediction and to what extent text can represent the score-related image contents. This work addresses these questions from an information-flow perspective by comparing existing BIQA models with three paradigms designed to learn the image–text–score relationship: Chain-of-Thought, Self-Consistency, and Autoencoder.

arxiv-2602-23740.title: An investigation on the FWHM of absorption features of type Ia supernovae
arxiv-2602-23740.creator: Xulin Zhao, Keiichi Maeda, Xiaofeng Wang
arxiv-2602-23740.description: Abstract We present an investigation of the full width at half maximum (FWHM, or γ \gamma ) of absorption features of Type Ia supernova (SNe Ia). We found that, the average value of FWHM can be well predicted with the rest wavelength ( λ \lambda ).

arxiv-2604-17132.title: Please refuse to answer me! Mitigating Over-Refusal in Large Language Models via Adaptive Contrastive Decoding
arxiv-2604-17132.creator: Yupeng Qi, Ziyu Lyu †, Lixin Cui, Lu Bai, Feng Xia

pmc-11116254.title: Exploring perceptions and experiences of stigma in Canada during the COVID-19 pandemic: a qualitative study
pmc-11116254.creator: Jeanette Cooper, Suvabna Theivendrampillai, Taehoon (Tom) Lee, Christine Marquez, Michelle Wai Ki Lau, Sharon E Straus, Christine Fahim, in partnership with the Chinese Canadian National Council Toronto Chapter, the Chinese Canadian National Council for Social Justice
pmc-11116254.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic fueled stigmatization and discrimination, particularly towards individuals of Chinese or East Asian ethnicity. We conducted interviews with members of the public in Canada in order to describe and understand stigma perceptions and experiences during the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-12533270.title: Hemorrhagic cystitis induced by intravenous esketamine in the treatment of new-onset refractory status epilepticus in children: a case report
pmc-12533270.creator: Jin-Meng Ding, Hong-Jun Miao, Yao Liu
pmc-12533270.description: IntroductionEsketamine, the S-enantiomer of ketamine, has been considered for terminating new-onset refractory status epilepticus (NORSE). However, there is limited large-scale data on its safety and comparative effectiveness. Ketamine-associated cystitis (KAC) is a known complication of chronic recreational ketamine use; however, there are few reports of cystitis caused by intravenous esketamine in children.

pmc-12583534.title: Molecular epidemiological characteristics of coxsackievirus A6 in Jinhua, China, 2019–2023
pmc-12583534.creator: Pengkai Sun, Zhifeng Pang, Bing Zhang, Junli Zhu, Bing Wu, Junling Wang, Xiaojing Yao, Shuying Zhu
pmc-12583534.description: We aimed to perform a retrospective analysis of the molecular epidemiological characteristics and genetic features of hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) associated with coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6) infections in Jinhua city from 2019 to 2023. Throat swab specimens were collected and tested. Two hundred CVA6-positive samples with viral loads>1 copies/µL were randomly selected for VP1 sequence amplification and sequencing.

pmc-12657435.title: Correlation of cognitive dysfunctions and diffusion tensor MRI measures in subjects with RRMS
pmc-12657435.creator: Alessio Mirabile, Carla Susinna, Giovanni Luca Cipriano, Giangaetano D’Aleo, Carmela Rifici, Edoardo Sessa, Angelo Quartarone, Viviana Lo Buono
pmc-12657435.description: BackgroundCognitive dysfunction is a common impairment observed in individuals with Multiple Sclerosis (MS), affecting key domains such as attention, information processing speed, memory, and executive functions. This deficit is typically identified through comprehensive neuropsychological assessments, which represent the gold standard for cognitive evaluation.

pmc-12676171.title: Contrast-Linked Pseudomonas Outbreak in a Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory
pmc-12676171.creator: Asadullah Bugti, Muhammad Kashif, Nousheen Aijaz, Moiz Ahmed Khan, Bashir Hanif
pmc-12676171.description: BackgroundInfection control breaches in cardiac catheterization laboratories are rare but may lead to severe consequences. Despite being a high-volume center and an award-winning participant in the national cardiovascular data registry Chest Pain MI registry, Tabba Heart Institute experienced a cluster of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections after coronary procedures.

pmc-12743086.title: ECSCR functions as a potential tumor suppressor in breast cancer cells
pmc-12743086.creator: Sen Lian, Yi Huang, Ling Liang, Yiping Yang, Yingxi Mo, Shan Wang, Changyuan Wei
pmc-12743086.description: Breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed malignancy among women worldwide. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), a particularly aggressive subtype, is unresponsive to endocrine and targeted therapies. It is characterized by high rates of invasion and recurrence, a poor prognosis, and limited treatment options. Resveratrol, a natural polyphenolic compound, possesses well-documented anticancer properties.

pmc-12859996.title: Giant galactocele in an adult female: a rare presentation and surgical management
pmc-12859996.creator: Getahun Jiru Bedada, Dereje Gebisa Bedada, Temesgen Regasa Gemeda, Ayana Guto Bone, Diriba Shiferaw Negese
pmc-12859996.description: BackgroundGalactocele, also known as lactocele, is a retention cyst resulting from lactiferous duct occlusion that typically occurs during lactation. Although a galactocele can occur anywhere along the milk line extending from the axilla to the groin, it has a propensity to form in the retroareolar region of the breasts.

pmc-13278921.title: Epidemiology, outcomes of treatment, and survival of cervical cancer in Kazakhstan: a nationwide population-based study
pmc-13278921.creator: Aidana Rakhmankulova, Yesbolat Sakko, Abduzhappar Gaipov, Kuralay Atageldiyeva, Talshyn Ukybassova, Assem Suleimenova, Yerbolat Iztleuov, Gulzhanat Aimagambetova
pmc-13278921.description: BackgroundCervical cancer remains one of the major medical and public health issues in Kazakhstan. In 2024, Kazakhstan launched a campaign to vaccinate 11- to 13-year-old girls, demonstrating successful implementation. This is a retrospective, population-based study aiming to investigate epidemiology, treatment outcomes, and survival of the cervical cancer pre-vaccination trends in a 10-year period (2014–2023).

pmc-13324592.title: Multitargeted Neuroprotective Strategies of Ethyl Pyruvate: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Perspectives in CNS Disorders
pmc-13324592.creator: Seung-Woo Kim, Hong Seok Kim
pmc-13324592.description: Ethyl pyruvate (EP), a simple aliphatic ester of pyruvic acid, is a potent neuroprotective compound with diverse properties, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-apoptotic, and metabolic regulatory activities. Given the intricate nature of neurological disorders, the multi-target mechanism of action of EP offers significant therapeutic advantages.

pmc-13508365.title: Paraventricular oxytocin neurons attenuate post-ischemic brain injury by suppressing microglia-mediated neuroinflammation
pmc-13508365.creator: Rui Liu, Xinyu Yang, Haozhi Gong, Huijie Fang, Xuebing Feng, Jiayao Li, Wentao Gao, Xiaoting Liang, Yanping Shen, Yubo Wang, Wei Wang, Jiaqi Jin, Liqun Jiao

pmc-13562659.title: Topological Fermi arc interference on low-symmetry Weyl surfaces
pmc-13562659.creator: Cong Li, Zhilong Yang, Hongxiong Liu, Magnus H. Berntsen, Francesco Scali, Dibya Phuyal, Jianfeng Zhang, Timur K. Kim, Jacek Osiecki, Balasubramanian Thiagarajan, Youguo Shi, Tao Xiang, Quansheng Wu, Oscar Tjernberg
pmc-13562659.description: Topological materials are defined by the correspondence between bulk topology and boundary states, yet this correspondence becomes enigmatic on low-symmetry surfaces where bulk and surface periodicities may not coincide within a conventional first bulk Brillouin zone projection. Here we study the (103) surface of the Weyl semimetal NdAlSi and identify Fermi arc interference in the boundary spectrum.

pmc-13575707.title: Measurement and modeling of diffuse ultraviolet radiation: A review
pmc-13575707.creator: Alfio V Parisi, Joanna Turner, Abdurazaq Amar, Damien P Igoe, Peter Schouten, Nawin Raj, Nathan Downs, Harry Butler
pmc-13575707.description: The ultraviolet (UV) radiation environment consists of direct UV and diffuse UV components. The ratios of diffuse‐to‐direct UV for the UVB, UVA, and the erythema UV wavebands are influenced by clouds, aerosols, albedo, and surface reflectance, Rayleigh scattering, and solar zenith angle.

pmc-13628252.title: Molecular epidemiological surveillance of the feline coronavirus reveals novel recombinant FCoV strains with evidence of ongoing viral evolution
pmc-13628252.creator: Abid Ullah Shah, Csaba Vagra, Nadine Moawad, Megan Rosen, Diane Levitan, Maged Gomaa Hemida
pmc-13628252.description: Highlights•Whole-genome sequencing identified three FCoV viral genomes (FIPV-170, FIPV-193, and FIPV-246) that belong to FCoV type-I.•These FCoV viral genomes shared about 90% nucleotide similarity with FCoV type-I strains and approximately 83% similarity with FCoV type-II strains, indicating substantial genomic drift.

uslaw-usc-t21-s2107.description: United States Code, Title 21 (Food And Drugs); Chapter 26 (Food Safety). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
